sections.title: The Dog and the Tortoise

dialogue.line: Once upon a time, a tortoise called out a dog for a race.

dialogue.speaker: Tortoise
dialogue.line: I can run faster than you.

dialogue.speaker: Dog
dialogue.line: You? You must be joking! Even in my sleep, you cannot run faster than me.

The tortoise planned to prepare large chunks of delicious meat with fat bones. He deliberately dropped the pieces of meat along the paths of the race thinking that the dog would smell the meat and get attracted to them.

illustrations: A large dog standing next to a small tortoise on a green field

sections.title: The Race

dialogue.line: On the day of their race, the other animals gathered to watch the most interesting race. As soon as the race started, the dog flew past the tortoise with high speed while the tortoise picked his steps as slowly and clumsily as he could.
Soon, the dog saw a chunk of meat on the way.

dialogue.speaker: Dog
dialogue.line: I will take a bite of this tasty meat before that slowcoach comes here.

As soon as he finished eating that meat, a few paces ahead he saw another piece on his path. So he slowed down and stopped to eat each piece. When the dog finally reached the finishing line, he met the tortoise there. He was surprised to see the tortoise before him and all the other animals praising the tortoise for winning the race.

illustrations: The tortoise at the finish line surrounded by other animals, the dog arriving in surprise

sections.title: Okon and Akan

dialogue.line: Once upon a time Okon, a farmer, went to check his traps. As he went near one of the traps, he noticed something caught in the trap which he could not see clearly. He called his friend, Akan, to help him remove the catch from the trap. Akan realised that the animal in the trap was a large snake which had gone to hide behind the stem of the trap.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: It is a large snake and this type spits!

dialogue.speaker: Okon
dialogue.line: Hold it by the tail.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: The trap caught it by the tail!

dialogue.speaker: Okon
dialogue.line: Then catch it by the head.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: Do you want it to bite me?

illustrations: Two men (Okon and Akan) standing near a wooden fence by a small building

sections.title: Okon and Akan (continued)

dialogue.speaker: Okon
dialogue.line: This snake does not bite, it only spits into people's eyes.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: Oh, ho! You want me to be blind? It is your trap. So go ahead and take your catch.

dialogue.speaker: Okon
dialogue.line: I know now that you are not a good friend.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: You are a true friend who wants me to be hurt.
The two men stood there looking at the large beast until it struggled out of the trap and crawled away into the jungle.

sections.title: Kabir and the Black Bag

dialogue.line: One bright morning, Kabir was going to his father's farm near which is located near their thatched house. On his way to the farm, he was thinking of the number of yam heaps he would have to make before noon. Then he would have to quickly bathe and rush to the local school that usually start at three.
He did not know if his mother would be able to give him food that day. He was only sure of the meal in the evening.

illustrations: Kabir walking to the farm, thinking about yams

What did he see under the leaves?

sections.title: The Black Bag

dialogue.line: Before Kabir went to the big kolanut tree that was very closeby to his father's farm, he noticed a black bag under the low leaves beside the path.
What could this be?
dialogue.speaker: Kabir

dialogue.line: He ran to the farm without looking back. When he was coming back, he noticed that the black bag was still there.
It must belong to someone. He must have been forgotten there. I must see what is inside. Perhaps I can get a clue of who the owner is.
dialogue.speaker: Kabir

dialogue.line: Kabir carefully opened the bag and found bundles of money neatly tied together with strong strings. He had never seen that much money in his entire life. He picked the bag and ran to the police station to handover the bag with money. The policemen were amazed at the honesty of a poor boy. Soon, the police found the owner of the bag. The man was so pleased with Kabir that he decided to pay his school fees.

sections.title: The Caterpillar and its Palace (Story)

dialogue.line: Once upon a time, all the animals used to live together. One day they found a palace in the jungle that they thought that nobody was living in it. The big animals like lions, tigers, hippopotamuses, elephants, and even smaller animals like the antelopes and squirrels started to argue among themselves about who was the most powerful and the bravest and the fittest to live in the palace.
As they continued to argue, they heard a loud voice from the palace saying;

I have ridden on elephants and rhinoceroses and lions and tigers and have broken their backs. I have proved to them that they are not as strong as they claimed. And the birds are afraid of me even though they can fly, I make their lives miserable if they come close to me. And so, if you dare enter this palace, be prepared for your death. But if you wish to dare death, make sure you do not come inside the palace with any bird.
dialogue.speaker: Voice

dialogue.line: The animals got frightened. They all ran away and did not live together again. From that day onwards, the caterpillar lived peacefully all alone in its big palace, the cocoon.

sections.title: The Fox and the Cock (Story)

dialogue.line: Many years ago, all the animals lived together except the fox. He said that unless he was made their king, no animal would be safe. So all the other animals planned to have a meeting on what they were going to do to tame or beg him.
On the agreed day for the meeting, all the animals met in the jungle square where all important decisions were usually taken. The animal who was asked to speak first then started.
We shall decide on what we shall do in order to make the fox happy.
dialogue.speaker: Speaker

illustrations: A fox standing next to a cock

questions: What did the fox want the animals to make him?

sections.title: The Fox and the Cock (Conclusion)

dialogue.line: The tortoise, who was a friend to the cock, told the meeting that the cock could not come but he would accept any decision of the other animals.
As the cock is not here, we shall tell the fox to take and eat up any cock he finds anywhere and at any time.
dialogue.speaker: Speaker

dialogue.line: All the animals agreed, and ever since then the cock and his relations became the easiest prey for the fox.

sections.title: Fat Head, Thin Legs, and Fat Cheeks

dialogue.line: Once upon a time, there lived three boys in a far village called Notedu. These boys were friends. They planned to steal mangoes from a farm close to their village on a work-free day when the owner of the mango trees would be sleeping at home.

sections.title: The Boys and the Mangoes

dialogue.line: When they got to the mango field, Fat Head said that he would be the one to climb the tree. The two others agreed with him. So, he climbed the tree and started shaking the branches. All the ripe mangoes began to drop one by one. After some time, Fat Head looked down from the height to see that Thin Legs and Fat Cheeks were hiding any mangoes. As he did so, his heavy head suddenly fell off from his body. Fat Cheeks began to laugh loudly that his cheeks burst open. Out of fear, Thin Legs began to run back home in order to say what had happened to the other two. But before he could reach home, his legs broke.
At the end, none of them ate the mangoes and none got home to tell the story of what happened to Fat Head, Thin Legs and Fat Cheeks.

sections.title: The Fishwoman (Story)

dialogue.line: A very long time ago, there lived a mermaid in the depths of the River Niger. The natives of Oma heard that she always came out at night but no one believed this story.

One dark night, Odika was walking down from Ebu, a nearby village. When he was walking close to the river, he heard some beautiful Allor Music coming out of the waters. He stopped to enjoy and learn the music so that it could be played when he was going to get the new title. He stepped forward a little closer. There was a huge mermaid near the river bank. She was very beautiful and her body shone as if there were lights all over her body. On seeing that Odika was not afraid. The mermaid turned and commanded him to come closer to her. Odika walked closer to the mermaid.

illustrations: A woman sitting next to a basket of fish

sections.title: Two Foolish Goats (Story)

dialogue.line: Two goats were running away from their greedy masters and met each other in the middle of the log of wood that the villagers on either side of the stream used as a bridge. None of them wanted to go back as they found it difficult to walk backwards. They were not wise enough to think on how to cross that narrow log. Then they started to argue.

sections.title: The Lion and the Soldier Ants (Story)

dialogue.line: The lion claimed that he was the king of all the animals. He took joy in roaring so that all the animals would continue to get afraid of him. The smaller animals and the soldier ants were thinking of what to do with the lion.
Let us enter his den at night.
dialogue.speaker: Head Soldier Ant

dialogue.line: Yes, that is right. We shall teach him a lesson.
dialogue.speaker: Mother Soldier Ant

questions: How did the lion always make the smaller animals afraid?
What did the soldier ants plan to do?
Who led the attack on the lion?
What did they want the lion to say?

What thing about lion did you learn from this story?
sections.title: The Lion and the Soldier Ants (Conclusion)

dialogue.line: We shall attack him the way we work. Some of you will enter his nostrils, some his ears, some his eyes and others will swarm all over his body. Bite him everywhere until he says that he is no longer the king of all animals. Do you hear me?
dialogue.speaker: Mother Soldier Ant

dialogue.line: Yes.
dialogue.speaker: Soldier Ants

dialogue.line: On that night, millions of soldier ants attacked the lion and started to bite him fiercely.
Oh Lion. Don't get proud of yourself. If you agree that you are no longer the king of all animals then we will set you free.
dialogue.speaker: Mother Soldier Ant

dialogue.line: I am the king of all animals.
dialogue.speaker: Lion

dialogue.line: Then we shall eat you raw. Children, eat as much of the lion as you like. He is very stubborn.
dialogue.speaker: Mother Soldier Ant

dialogue.line: I am still the king of all animals.
dialogue.speaker: Lion

dialogue.line: When the soldier ants had eaten off all the flesh in the stomach and back of the lion, the lion cried that he is no longer the king of all the animals. He had only hair on his head. And that is why the lion has a mane.

sections.title: The Elephant and his Master (Story)

dialogue.line: In a far village of Sambesi, there lived a family of twenty elephants and their master called Hamsaki. Hamsaki had a wife and five children who made the elephants do all kinds of work on the farm, and for other villagers who wanted some fast jobs to be done.
The human beings we work for, are much smaller than us in size. Why should we be serving them? From today, any human being who comes here will be made to serve us.
dialogue.speaker: Mother Elephant

dialogue.line: How can you do that?
dialogue.speaker: Young Elephant

dialogue.line: Never mind. I will put my weight on the first person who comes here and then I will force others to do what I demand or I will crush that person with just one stamping.
dialogue.speaker: Mother Elephant

dialogue.line: I see. I did not know that we have such huge power to make Hamsaki serve us.
dialogue.speaker: Young Elephant

dialogue.line: On that morning it was Hamsaki who came there first. The mother elephant placed him on the floor and put his left foot on his chest while waiting for the other members of the family to come out. But Hamsaki died due to the heavy weight of the elephant's foot.

illustrations: Hamsaki standing next to a large elephant

questions: How many elephants were there in the family?
In which village were they all living?
What did the elephants want human beings to do?

sections.title: The Elephant and his Master (Conclusion)

dialogue.line: On seeing this, the members of Hamsaki's family got frightened and they ran away to another village. The elephants did not have anyone to feed them any more. And as from that day onwards, elephants became wild animals.
